mechanism.name: Binary instrumental variable model with a nonlinear complier effect curve

sampling.dependence: iid individuals. One active scalar x~U(-1,1); Z depends on x, and D/Y are sampled jointly conditional on x,Z. Binary principal-stratum model without interference.

assumptions: Consistency, well-defined interventions, independent individuals and no interference.
A2 conditional IV independence: Z independent of potential outcomes and potential treatments given x.
A3 conditional IV relevance: nonzero complier probability.
A4 IV positivity on the declared bounded covariate support.
Correct tanh curve model for the transformed-curve slope target; no need to identify never-takers treated or always-takers untreated outcomes.

properties.notes: One genuinely active scalar baseline x; the source vector (1,x) contains an intercept, which is not counted as a random covariate. Nonlinearity is tanh(alpha0+alpha1*x), four expit links, exp(eta0+eta1*x), and the joint-probability inverse map. No explicit covariate-product interaction is added. D,Y dependence is not an added regression interaction. Baseline-dimension convention: p=1, effective_p=1, baseline_columns=['x']; instruments, posttreatment variables, time points and network nodes are excluded. Reference sample size n_ref=128 independent subjects (the CPU interface-check setting), p/n_ref=0.00781250; high_dimensional=false refers to baseline p in this stated setting, not the full observed-column count. n remains a runtime argument; reassess the dimension/sample-size regime if n or p changes rather than treating this tag as a guarantee for arbitrary scaling.

estimand.name: alpha1
estimand.definition: Slope alpha1 in atanh(delta_L(x))=alpha0+alpha1*x, where delta_L(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)|D(1)>D(0),x]. Potential outcomes contrast D=1 versus D=0 among conditional compliers. Equivalently [atanh(delta_L(0.5))-atanh(delta_L(-0.5))]/1.0 under the declared curve model. This parameter is not a risk difference itself and is not the population ATE.

truth.expression: Slope alpha1 in atanh(delta_L(x))=alpha0+alpha1*x, where delta_L(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)|D(1)>D(0),x]. Potential outcomes contrast D=1 versus D=0 among conditional compliers. Equivalently [atanh(delta_L(0.5))-atanh(delta_L(-0.5))]/1.0 under the declared curve model. This parameter is not a risk difference itself and is not the population ATE.
truth.derivation: Analytic alpha1=-1, the slope of atanh(LATE(x)); independently recovered by principal-stratum mixture, odds-product bisection and conditional Wald inversion; not population ATE or raw LATE.

adaptations: Keep the additive Section 5 observed-data probability law and all its numeric parameters from the explicitly read arXiv v2. Only this single DGP scenario is declared; nuisance-model fitting variants are not separate DGPs.

Scalar collection interface reports the original curve parameter alpha1, the slope of atanh(LATE(x)), rather than the full two-component alpha vector or the entire curve. No new causal target population or intervention is introduced.

Return scalar x without the deterministic intercept column. Reconstruct the same observed joint law using Supplement S1 and a new local Python RNG categorical inverse CDF; author RNG and Monte Carlo outputs are not reproduced.
